summary.text: 楼 is the simplified form of 樓, a character for a building with two or more storeys. In 樓, 木 marks a wood-related meaning category and 婁 supplies the sound; simplified 楼 uses 娄 in place of 婁.

formation.text: The traditional graph 樓 is phonosemantic: 木 contributes a wood-related meaning category, while 婁 serves as the phonetic element. In simplified 楼, 娄 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 婁.

components.text: 木 is the left component in 楼 and 樓. In 樓 it marks a wood-related meaning category; the account does not specify a narrower connection to the building.
娄 is the right component in 楼 and the standardized simplified counterpart of 婁 in 樓. Its modern Mandarin reading matches 楼, supporting its phonetic role in the simplified graph.

sound.text: 娄 and 楼 share the modern Mandarin reading lóu.

components.text: 婁 is the right component of 樓 and is identified as its phonetic element. Both are read lóu in modern Mandarin. The available Old Chinese reconstructions use different systems, so they are not a direct historical comparison.

sound_limitation.text: The Baxter–Sagart data give a reconstruction for 婁 but no entry for 樓; the cited Old Chinese reconstruction for 樓 is from Zhengzhang’s system. These data do not provide a same-system historical comparison.

sound.text: 婁 and 樓 share the modern Mandarin reading lóu.
The reported Old Chinese forms are 婁 *[r]o in Baxter–Sagart and 樓 *ɡ·roː in Zhengzhang. Because they come from different systems, they are not a direct comparison.
sound.system: Old Chinese; Baxter–Sagart for 婁 and Zhengzhang for 樓

history.text: The traditional graph 樓 is recorded with 木 and 婁 and explained as a building with two or more storeys. A small-seal form and manuscript examples are also recorded, but their dates and the graph’s earliest attestation are unresolved.
楼 is the standardized simplified form of 樓, with 娄 in place of 婁. The simplification is undated; the separate account of 婁’s history does not show that the substitution resulted from copying error.

uncertainties.text: The graph’s earliest attestation and a complete early sequence of its forms are unresolved, although its traditional construction and basic meaning are supported.

婁 is identified as the phonetic element in 樓, and both share the modern Mandarin reading lóu. The cited Old Chinese reconstructions use different systems, and the Baxter–Sagart data contain no entry for 樓.

senses.gloss: building with two or more storeys
senses.text: The traditional account gives this as the basic meaning and the earliest sense supported here; it does not establish that this was the graph’s first historical meaning.

senses.gloss: upper structure on a vehicle, ship, or wall
senses.text: Cited examples use 樓 for elevated structures on vehicles, ships, or walls. Their dates and relationship to the multistorey-building sense are unresolved.
A cited literary example uses 樓 for a building storey; when this use arose is unresolved.

senses.gloss: commercial or entertainment premises, including teahouses or taverns
senses.text: Cited examples use 樓 for premises such as teahouses or taverns. They do not establish when this use arose or how it relates to the other senses.

senses.gloss: building of two or more stories
senses.text: The current definition retains the multistorey-building sense.
Japanese references list watchtower and lookout meanings; their development from the traditional basic sense is unresolved.

limitations.text: The examples show several uses but do not establish a dated sequence or transitions among multistorey buildings, elevated structures, building storeys, and commercial premises.
The cited Japanese lexical dates concern Japanese uses; they do not date the Chinese graph or the origin of corresponding Chinese senses.

components.text: 木 marks the wood-related meaning category in the traditional construction.
娄 occupies 婁’s place in simplified 楼.
婁 is the sound-bearing part of traditional 樓.

relationships.text: 木 contributes the meaning category in the traditional construction carried into 楼.
娄 supplies the phonetic element in simplified 楼. 娄 and 楼 share the modern Mandarin reading lóu; 娄 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 婁 in traditional 樓.
